Middle East.headline: WHO Reports 4,481 Casualties and 181,000 Displaced in Yemen Since August
Middle East.body: The World Health Organization has reported a severe deterioration in Yemen’s humanitarian and health conditions, citing 4,481 casualties and over 181,000 displaced persons since the beginning of August due to escalating military conflicts in Lahj, Marib, and Taiz. According to the fifth field report issued by the Health Cluster in coordination with the WHO, the death toll has reached 838, with the total number of casualties climbing by 800 in just one week. This surge represents an average of nearly 100 new injuries reported daily. Middle East.headline: Yemen escalation fuels fears of further cholera, measles spread
Middle East.body: Yemen escalation fuels fears of further cholera, measles spread Heavy fighting in Yemen is fuelling concerns of an uptick in cholera, measles and other preventable diseases, as overcrowding at displacement sites threatens to overwhelm the limited healthcare services still open. “We know that comprehensive emergency obstetric and newborn care has been suspended in two hospitals, in Marib and Ras Al-Arah, because staff and operating capacities have been redirected to trauma care to care for the incoming wounded,” said Dr Annette Heinzelmann, UN World Health Organization (WHO) Regional Emergency Director for the Eastern Mediterranean. Americas.headline: Flooding, power cuts and evacuations as Hurricane Polo slams Mexico
Americas.body: Power was cut to part of Mexico's Baja California peninsula on Monday as Hurricane Polo prepared to roar ashore on the Pacific Coast, causing flooding as the sea breached coastal defenses. The Category 3 storm is the first hurricane of this year's season that will make landfall, turbo-charged by the El Nino weather phenomenon which has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific. Polo was on the cusp of tearing across the south of Baja California with heavy rain and hurricane-force winds, the US National Hurricane Center (NHC) said. Americas.body: Canada extends travel restrictions linked to Ebola outbreak for 60 days Posted September 28, 2026 3:06 pm. Last Updated September 28, 2026 4:16 pm. OTTAWA — Canada has extended its travel and immigration restrictions related to the Ebola outbreak for another 60 days, and the health ministry in the Democratic Republic of Congo has released new data showing there have been more than 8,000 cases of the virus. People from Uganda, South Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo have been barred from travelling to Canada since May. Africa.headline: Ebola cases surpass 8,000 as DRC struggles to control outbreak
Africa.body: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has recorded over 8,000 cases of Ebola, including almost 4,000 deaths, amid the worst outbreak in the country’s history, according to government data. The latest report, published on Monday by the DRC’s public health institute, put the number of cases at 8,067 and deaths at 3,901, representing a fatality rate of 48.4 percent.

Africa.headline: Conflict-driven displacement threatens DRC Ebola response
Africa.body: Security incidents have been reported at Kigonze displacement camp in Bunia, Ituri province, since September 20. Reports indicate that soldiers entered the site to search for weapons and people suspected of belonging to non-state armed groups. Gunfire was also heard. The United Nations (UN) Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs said residents had faced armed violence, threats, intimidation, arrests, forced displacement and destruction of shelters. Kigonze hosted nearly 19 000 displaced people. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Protecting women and girls against sexual abuse, exploitation during the Ebola outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo—Every few days, Esperance Ayikoro walks through the bustling Cinquantenaire Market in Bunia, the capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s eastern Ituri Province, stopping to speak with women selling food and household items. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola outbreak tops 8,000 confirmed cases as disease remains out of control
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The number of confirmed cases of Ebola virus in The Democratic Republic of the Congo has surged past 8,000, as the country runs out of health workers to contain the deadly disease. DR Congo announced an outbreak on May 15, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, which has no known treatment or vaccine, and has struggled to contain it. Latest data from DR Congo’s health ministry showed that 8,067 cases have been confirmed, with 3,901 deaths as of September 26 across 63 health zones in seven of the country’s 26 provinces, with a fatality rate of more than 48%. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: NCoS Contains Cholera Outbreak At Kano Custodial Centre
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: The Nigerian Correctional Service (NCoS) has confirmed that a recent cholera outbreak at the Kurmawa Medium Security Custodial Centre in Kano has been contained, although two people died from the disease. The outbreak was confirmed through laboratory investigations on September 23, 2026, by the NCoS medical team at the facility in collaboration with Kano State public health authorities. In a statement by the Service Public Relations Officer, Jane Osuji, the Controller-General of Corrections, Sylvester Ndidi Nwakuche, who was immediately briefed, directed that all necessary measures be sustained to protect the lives, health and welfare of inmates and personnel. Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Stay with the Eyewitness News AccuWeather team for continuing updates. NEW YORK CITY (WABC) -- A powerful nor'easter brought flooding, strong winds and dangerous ocean conditions to parts of New York City on Saturday, toppling trees and leaving residents in waterfront communities cleaning up damage while officials warned that worsening conditions could be on the way. The strong winds caused havoc in Glendale, Queens, where a tree came down at 76-12 88th St. between 77th and 76th avenues around 5:40 p.m., leaving the roadway blocked off because of downed power lines.
